product.summary: Develops and manufactures ultra-precision, high-speed Fast Steering Mirrors (FSM) and optical acquisition, pointing, and tracking (PAT) platforms needed for laser communications between satellites, satellite-to-ground, and defense systems such as laser weapons.
product.problem_statement: Laser communication between low-Earth orbit satellites requires precise targeting of a small receiver thousands of kilometers away. The FSM, a core component that maintains a stable beam despite vibrations, thermal deformation, and satellite attitude changes, has been entirely dependent on foreign companies such as Germany's PI. There is an urgent need for high-reliability, high-shock-resistant FSMs tailored to domestic satellite and defense demand.
product.solution: Developed both piezo and voice coil FSMs in-house. The voice coil type achieves a range of ±18 mrad (max), while the piezo type achieves a control accuracy of 0.6 µrad and a resonance frequency of approximately 1,900 Hz. Completed development of a space-grade FSM in December 2025, passed ground-based space environment tests, and is currently undergoing actual space environment verification aboard the 5th launch of Nuri in October 2026.
key_features: Voice coil FSM: 25mm mirror diameter, maximum ±18 mrad deflection range, 10 µrad control accuracy
Piezo FSM: 25mm diameter, 50g weight, 0.6 µrad control accuracy
KQS 9100 (Aerospace and Defense Quality Management System) certification obtained
In-house space environment testing facilities (vibration, thermal vacuum) established
Expanding product lineup to include Laser Steering Systems (LCT) and PAT modules
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The only domestic FSM company with dual technology platforms: piezoelectric (Piezo) and electromagnetic (Voice Coil) actuation. Core technologies include precision actuation and control algorithms and optimization for resistance to space environments (vibration, radiation, temperature changes). Currently developing a PAT system through a Scale-Up TIPS R&D project (total KRW 1.2B) awarded in 2025.
product.target_customer: Domestic and international space and defense companies (e.g., Hanwha Systems), national research institutions (KARI, KASA), satellite communication operators (LEO constellations), and laser weapon system developers.
product.business_model: B2B supply of FSM components and PAT subsystems. Revenue generated through custom design and manufacturing per customer specifications. Aims to enter overseas supply chains after establishing mass production systems.

direct_competitors.comparison: Germany-based global FSM market leader. Has a track record (space heritage) of embedding FSMs in numerous satellites. Incerasolution is challenging with its own technology for the first time in South Korea.
France-based FSM and adaptive optics specialist. Has a MEMS-based FSM lineup. Incerasolution responds with its dual piezo and voice coil platform.
Supplies FSMs for research and industrial use. Stronger in the research and laboratory market than in space-grade applications.
Specialized in MEMS-type FSMs. Advantages include small size and low cost, but limited space certification track record.
Major U.S. defense conglomerate. Produces satellite optical communication terminals and FSMs in-house. Has overwhelming advantages in scale and capital compared to Incerasolution.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: The only domestic company independently developing and manufacturing FSMs. Covers both piezo and voice coil methods with a dual technology platform. Has a track record of supplying actual domestic defense customers such as Hanwha Systems. Securing space heritage through the 5th Nuri launch.
competitive_landscape.moat: High barriers to entry for space and defense FSMs (shock resistance, radiation resistance, temperature tolerance, military security, quality certification). Incerasolution has obtained KQS 9100 certification, been selected for consecutive government projects, and secured anchor domestic customers like Hanwha Systems, enabling initial market entry. The government's space component localization policy provides strong backing.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The global market is dominated by Germany's PI, France's Alpao, and the U.S.'s L3Harris, but in the domestic space and defense market, Incerasolution is the only native supplier. With the government's space component localization policy and explosive growth in the LEO satellite communication market, the strategy is to build a domestic base and then expand overseas. Lacks scale and space heritage compared to global top-tier companies, but is targeting a niche with verification through the Korean launch vehicle (Nuri) and competitive pricing and customization.

Gaining attention amid a macro trend where the space optical communication market is growing 25–30% annually.

product.summary: Develops WIM, an ultra-lightweight (1.6kg) walking assist wearable robot, and ALLEX, an upper-body humanoid robot based on back-drivable technology. A data-hardware virtuous cycle where real human gait data accumulated from WIM is used for ALLEX's control algorithms.
product.problem_statement: Existing wearable robots are heavy (3-4kg+), making daily wear difficult, and humanoids rely on expensive external force/torque sensors, resulting in high manufacturing costs and limited safe physical interaction with humans.
product.solution: WIM uses the world's first single-motor (single-actuator) system to achieve 1.6kg weight, wearable in 30 seconds. ALLEX uses back-drivable actuators and proprietary motor control algorithms (integrated position, force, and stiffness control) to achieve full-body force sensing (100gf level) without external sensors, enabling a compliant humanoid.
key_features: WIM: 1.6kg ultra-lightweight, single actuator, 20% walking energy reduction, 6 modes (assist/resist/uphill/downhill/slow/hiking), AI gait analysis app, IP54 dust/water resistance

ALLEX: 48 degrees of freedom (15 DoF per hand), 100gf finger force sensing (sensorless), 40N fingertip force, 30kg+ hook grip strength, 0.3mm or less repeatability
ALLEX: Upper body approx. 5kg lightweight structure, 3kg+ one-hand payload (20kg-class collaborative robot level), EtherCAT-based real-time whole-body control
WIM Premium: Subscription-based software feature updates, customized assistive force adjustment for gait patterns
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Core technology is back-drivability — the motor's natural yielding to external forces. WIM's single actuator drives both sides simultaneously with a symmetrical assist frame. ALLEX combines low-friction, high-load actuators with gravity-compensating waist mechanism to detect subtle forces of 100gf. Integrated with AWS and NVIDIA Isaac simulation platforms.

product.summary: Develops chemical thrusters for satellites that use low-toxicity propellant and control combustion electrically. Combines the high thrust of conventional chemical thrusters with the control flexibility of electric thrusters.
product.problem_statement: Existing satellite thrusters have two limitations: (1) Chemical thrusters provide high thrust but have limited catalyst life, making refueling difficult; (2) Electric thrusters offer good fuel efficiency but low thrust, limiting rapid orbit changes. Additionally, traditional hydrazine propellant poses high toxicity and explosion risks, significantly increasing safety management costs.
product.solution: Technology for an 'electrically controlled chemical thruster' that directly decomposes and combusts propellant with electricity, eliminating the need for a catalyst. Ensures safety by synthesizing low-toxicity propellant in-house. Without a catalyst, satellite life can be extended by simply refueling propellant.
key_features: Catalyst-free, electrically controlled ignition, extinction, and thrust regulation
In-house synthesis of low-toxicity, high-safety propellant
High thrust comparable to chemical thrusters
On-orbit refueling capability (no catalyst life constraints)
Self-owned R&D capabilities from propellant synthesis to combustion and vacuum environment testing
